daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The KPK has detained the Bupati of Kuantan Singingi (Kuansing) in a major corruption case involving kickbacks from infrastructure projects and agricultural exploitation. The bupati previously received a Pajero as a bribe when serving as acting bupati, and during the latest operation the KPK also detained the bupati's second wife. The KPK revealed that the bupati extracted payments from farmers and stated the case tarnished the noble values of the region.

  • DPR Commission I approved ratification bills for defence cooperation agreements between Indonesia-Turkey and Indonesia-Malaysia.
  • DPR Commission II will not yet discuss revision of the Regional Election Law.
  • Golkar warned that military academy cadets training students at Sekolah Rakyat should not create an impression of militarism in the classroom.
  • Vice President Cak Imin said the process to write off JKN contribution arrears is being finalized.
  • President Prabowo stated that law must not become a tool for those with money or political revenge, and said Indonesia is at a historic turning point as major transformation begins.
  • Bawaslu in East Nusa Tenggara partnered with PWI to strengthen oversight ahead of the 2029 election.
  • Sixteen labour confederations formed a grand coalition to monitor implementation of the Labour Law.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs confirmed that two Indonesian crew members missing in South Korea have still not been found. Meanwhile, TNI Marines are participating in RIMPAC 2026, where they taught jungle survival techniques to military personnel from participating nations. The hajj minister officially closed the 2026 hajj operation, with Indonesia pledging service upgrades for future pilgrimages.

  • The hajj minister reported that 60 pilgrims remain hospitalized in Saudi Arabian hospitals.

Other

Finance Minister Purbaya signaled that Pertamax prices may decline and stated that June inflation was driven by volatile prices, not demand. Indonesia officially began the B50 biodiesel rollout at 29 terminals, with the government stating all sectors are ready for the July implementation. The government and ride-hailing companies agreed to protect the online transportation ecosystem, though some drivers reported mixed results after the 8 percent commission rate took effect.

  • The government delayed e-commerce fee increases for MSME merchants and plans to tighten enforcement against companies that do not provide BPJS coverage for employees.
  • The Ministry of Transportation strengthened cooperation with Organda on public transport safety culture and is pushing electrification of public transport.
  • Indonesia eyes the growing global Muslim travel market by 2030, while data showed domestic tourists spend more than foreign visitors and the country received 1.38 million foreign tourist arrivals in May.
  • Aceh is pushing Andaman gas downstreaming for economic growth while Indonesia eyes carbon incentives for green ports under the NEK scheme.
  • Pertamina and Pupuk Indonesia explored strategic collaboration to strengthen energy and food security.
